solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Change one's mind about slang

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for 'concerning' or 'about'
cant is the jargon or slang of a particular group

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders their view on the use of slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change one's mind about' reads as one phrase, but 'about' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a belief or statement formerly held, a formal kind of reversing opinion.

clue.text: Arab enemy to be destroyed before independence can begin

indicators.note: a word that is destroyed is broken up, so its letters are rearranged
the word that can begin is reduced to its opening letter

explanation.surface: An enemy must be crushed before a nation's independence can start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be destroyed' scrambles ENEMY into YEMEN; 'can begin' takes just the first letter of 'independence'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Yemen, on the Arabian peninsula, is an Arab, so this is an example of the broader term.

clue.text: Chaos and hell (men start to grumble) is entering a country

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, hence hell
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: a nation is a country
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pandemonium breaks out as grumbling men pour into a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes only the first letter of 'grumble'; 'entering' places the two-letter word just after the first letter of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorganisation, a lack of order or system, is a near synonym of chaos.

clue.text: The writer's tale given a new middle section — detective story?

parts.note: the writer, from the setter's point of view, is me, so the writer's is my

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a story is a tale

explanation.surface: An author's tale gets a fresh middle chapter, perhaps turning it into a whodunit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a new middle section' replaces the central O of STORY with E, making STERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery is a genre of fiction about solving a crime; the question mark flags it as one kind of detective story.

clue.text: Ruler of yesteryear — I haven't the answer to this clue?

parts.note: read the answer as instructions: its first two words are a terrible, that is jumbled, version of these two clue words

explanation.surface: A solver confesses they cannot crack this very clue.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: treat 'terrible' in the answer as an anagram signal applied to IVANTHE, and the letters rearrange to I HAVEN'T.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth-century tsar of Russia known by this epithet is a ruler from long ago.

clue.text: Very big hesitation follows support for one suggesting idea

indicators.note: the later pieces come after the first in the answer

parts.note: a prop is a support
OS is outsize, an abbreviation for very big clothing
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A huge pause comes after backing a person who puts forward a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposer is the person who puts forward a motion or suggestion for consideration.

clue.text: Running full, river in swampy area suits amphibian

indicators.note: the letters go inside the swampy word

parts.note: a bog is a marshy area

indicators.note: running water churns, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A brimming river flowing through marshland suits a creature living there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like part of the river picture but is the anagram signal; 'in' puts the result after the first letter of the swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfrog is a large frog, and frogs are amphibians, so this is an example of the class.

clue.text: Feature of hare — it hides in plant

indicators.note: the small word hides inside the plant's name

parts.note: celery is a plant

explanation.surface: A hare's characteristic lies concealed in a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides in' places the small word just before the plant's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is swiftness, and speed is the trait famously associated with the hare.

clue.text: Six with regret about wait ultimately showing patience?

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the regret word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Waiting with regret for six hours finally proves one's patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives T from 'wait'; 'about' wraps RUE round it as RTUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is one example of a moral virtue, which the question mark acknowledges.

clue.text: Music request made when No.1's slipped to No.3

indicators.note: the word's first letter drops down to third position

parts.note: to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A chart record falls from the top spot to third, prompting a request.
explanation.walkthrough: The A at the head of ASK slips to the end, giving the third position.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a style of Jamaican popular music, forerunner of reggae.

clue.text: A judge in one shoe, lacking a pair of them

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the footwear word

parts.note: a boot is a single item of footwear
ref, short for referee, is a judge in sport

explanation.surface: A judge wears only one shoe, missing the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' in the definition refers back to shoes, so the definition leans on the wordplay's 'shoe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Going barefoot means wearing no shoes at all, so without a pair of them.

clue.text: Inflammable liquid bringing destruction ultimately to a tree

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word

parts.note: a palm is a tree

explanation.surface: A burning fluid finally brings ruin to a single tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is a jellied petrol used in incendiary weapons, so a flammable fuel.

clue.text: Chorister's grant arranged by a group of musicians

indicators.note: musical arranging fits the surface, and here it reorders the letters

explanation.surface: A choirboy's grant is organised by an ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Chorister's' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble of violins, violas, cellos and basses is a band of players.

clue.text: Music events to raise money

definitions.meaning: a ... is a British students' charity fundraising event, such as ... week

explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime pieces are rags, and British universities hold annual charity stunts under the same name.

clue.text: Traveller in plane to get very angry

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
to rant is to rage angrily

explanation.surface: A passenger aboard an aircraft loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: the traveller is not inside the plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is someone who moves from place to place, so a traveller in the broad sense.

clue.text: Is ancient mischief-maker being imprisoned, unable to see others?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the mischief-maker is locked inside the other word

parts.note: old means ancient
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: An old troublemaker is jailed, cut off from fellow prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being imprisoned' locks the Greek goddess inside the word for ancient, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone isolated is cut off and alone, so able to meet no one else; the question mark admits the loose phrasing.

clue.text: Cart bringing fruit, heaps on top

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece on top comes first

parts.note: ricks are stacks or heaps of hay
a haw is the fruit of the hawthorn

explanation.surface: A wagon carrying fruit with piles stacked above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light two-wheeled vehicle pulled by a person, a kind of cart.

clue.text: Place I picked out for having gold and silver — in this!

definitions.text: Place I picked out for having gold and silver — in this!

indicators.note: having means containing, so the metals go inside
picked out means removed from the word

parts.note: a site is a place
or is heraldic gold
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A location chosen for keeping gold and silver: a vault, in fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked out' removes I, leaving STE, which 'having' wraps round the two metal symbols. The whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is space for keeping things safe, the very place to put precious metals.

clue.text: Get rid of brilliant performer when intrinsic value is reduced by 90%

indicators.text: when intrinsic value is reduced by 90%
indicators.note: the inner letter is a Roman hundred, cut by ninety per cent to a Roman ten

parts.note: an ace is an expert performer

explanation.surface: Fire a star when their real worth drops sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: The C (100) inside ACE becomes X (10), a cut of 90%.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe is to dismiss or scrap, as in axing a job or a programme.

clue.text: Porch with royal inscription in London museum

indicators.note: the royal letters go inside the museum's initials

parts.note: the V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is inscribed on royal items

explanation.surface: An entrance porch bearing a regal monogram is displayed in a London museum.
explanation.walkthrough: V&A is spelt out as V AND A, with ER after its V.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed platform along the outside of a house, a kind of porch.

clue.text: Team of cattle transporters blocking one's cart awkwardly

indicators.note: the scrambled piece blocks the middle of the other word by sitting inside it

parts.note: drovers drive cattle from place to place

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Cattle drovers get in the way of someone's clumsily handled cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges the letters, apostrophe dropped; 'blocking' puts them after the first letter of the drovers. Doncaster Rovers is an English football club from South Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Doncaster Rovers is a professional football club, so this is an example of a sports team.

clue.text: Canticle? Archdeacon wants it before end of service

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An archdeacon wants a hymn before the service ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venite is Psalm 95, sung as a canticle at Anglican morning prayer.

clue.text: Observe fish drowning in wine

indicators.note: the fish is submerged inside the wine word

parts.note: red is red wine
a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Watch a fish being drowned in wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drowning in' sinks the fish between the first and second letters of the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at or watch attentively.

clue.text: Boy's beginning to want girl back? One may be barking

indicators.note: a beginning is a first letter
back means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Tessa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A boy at the start wants his girlfriend back; is he crazy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TESSA into ASSET. 'Barking' also means mad in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hound, so a dog that barks.

clue.text: A legal right takes time — foreigner is in such a state

definitions.text: foreigner is in such a state

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Claiming a legal entitlement drags on, and the foreigner remains in limbo.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienage is the legal status of being an alien, the condition a foreign national is in.

clue.text: Particle of metal first bit of rubbing removed

indicators.note: the letter is taken away from the metal

parts.note: iron is a metal

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A speck of metal comes off on first rubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ion is an electrically charged atom or molecule, a particle in physics.

clue.text: Smooth ambassador ditching English love

indicators.note: ditching means dropping a letter from the word

parts.note: a legate is an envoy or ambassador
love is zero in tennis, hence O

explanation.surface: A suave diplomat dumps his English lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is a musical direction meaning played smoothly, with notes joined.

clue.text: Procrastinating, I had turned Liberal — subsequently a member of another party

indicators.note: turned means the contraction is turned round

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
a Tory is a member of the Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician dithers, having changed to Liberal and then to a rival party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory means slow or tending to delay, which is what putting things off amounts to.
